claims.text: The dynamic mechanical response of Co-free FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes is governed by the nucleation, growth, and dissolution kinetics of nanoscale CSRO clusters.
Nanoscale CSRO clusters modulate dislocation mobility in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
An intermediate regime exists in which the rate of CSRO reconfiguration matches the imposed strain rate.
Matching CSRO reconfiguration kinetics to the imposed strain rate enhances ductility without compromising strength.
Nanoscale CSRO clusters dynamically form, evolve, and dissolve during deformation of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
CSRO clusters act as transient obstacles to dislocation motion under dynamic loading.
Low temperatures and high strain rates reduce atomic mobility and hinder CSRO reconfiguration.
Hindered CSRO reconfiguration increases dislocation pinning.
Increased dislocation pinning produces higher yield strength and lower ductility.
Balancing CSRO formation and dissolution kinetics with dislocation activity produces a superior strength–ductility product.
Mechanical properties will vary non-monotonically with temperature and strain rate.
An intermediate temperature and strain-rate regime will retain high strength while providing greater ductility than low-temperature/high-rate and high-temperature/low-rate regimes.
At high temperature and low strain rate, excessive CSRO dissolution reduces strengthening.
Reversible changes in the degree of CSRO will correlate with changes in dislocation behavior and mechanical response.
Under quasi-static or conventional testing conditions, CSRO effects are static or less dynamically active.
Within cryogenic to approximately 300°C and strain rates of approximately 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1, CSRO dynamics are the proposed governing mechanism for minimally defective, arc-melted Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Outside the stated temperature, strain-rate, processing, and defect-state boundaries, additional deformation mechanisms may operate.
Twinning or transient phase transformations may overlap with and obscure the contribution of CSRO dynamics.
Rapid CSRO changes during deformation are technically challenging to detect.
